Testimony of Angela Westhoff, President & CEO Maine Health Care Association
Testimony before the Committee on Health and Human Services In Support of LD 1106, An Act to Provide Funds for the Redevelopment of the Island Nursing Home in
Hancock County into Affordable Senior Housing
Senator Curry and Representative Gere as well as Distinguished Members of the Committee on Housing and Economic Development:
My name is Angela Westhoff, and I serve as the President & CEO of the Maine Health Care Association. We represent approximately 200 nursing homes, assisted living centers, and residential care facilities across the state. Our mission is to empower members to ensure the integrity, quality, and sustainability of long term care in Maine.
I am providing written testimony in support of LD 1106, An Act to Provide Funds for the Redevelopment of the Island Nursing Home in Hancock County into Affordable Senior Housing. Over the last 10 years, Maine has lost 29 nursing homes. Hancock County has no nursing homes left. Half of Washington County's homes have closed since 2014. Just two months ago, another nursing home in Aroostook County announced it would have to close. Maine has the fewest skilled nursing home beds per 1,000 residents in the entire Northeastern United States. As the oldest state in the country, access to long term care and affordable housing for Maine's older adult population should be a top priority.
The closure of Island Nursing Home was devastating to the residents, the families, the staff and the community. Board members of the facility tried desperately to keep the facility open and they also explored options of trying to reopen as a residential care facility. However, the ongoing challenges of MaineCare reimbursement rates being so low that they do not cover the cost of care, coupled with a staffing shortage, were just too insurmountable. I urge the committee to consider the small investment needed to help redevelop the facility into affordable housing for older adults living in Hancock County. Thank you for your time.

Before the Housing and Economic Development Committee

Senator Curry, Representative Gere, and distinguished members of the Housing and Economic
Development Committee, my name is Representative Holly Eaton, and I proudly represent
House District 15, which includes the island and coastal communities of Deer Isle, Stonington, Brooklin, Tremont, Southwest Harbor, Frenchboro, Swan's Island, Isle au Haut, and Vinalhaven.
I am here today as the sponsor of LD 1106, "An Act to Provide Funds for the Redevelopment of the Island Nursing Home in Hancock County into Affordable Senior Housing."
LD 1106 proposes a one-time appropriation of $250,000 to the Maine State Housing Authority to
support the redevelopment of the former Island Nursing Home, located in Deer Isle, into 24
affordable apartments for senior citizens.
When the Island Nursing Home closed, it created a ripple effect that continues to impact families across our region. We lost a critical long-term care facility -- but more than that, we lost a sense of stability and safety for our aging residents. Many elders were forced to leave their island
homes and the communities they helped build, and our region has struggled to recover from that
loss.
Since the closure, the Board of Directors of the Island Nursing Home has remained committed to finding a path forward. I've been supportive of their efforts and am proud to bring forward this opportunity through LD 1106. The proposal to convert the facility into affordable senior housing
is both thoughtful and urgently needed. In coordinating with the Maine State Housing Authority, this bill provides the initial funding necessary to move the project toward construction.

District 15: Brooklin, Deer lsle, Eagle Island Township, Frenchboro, Southwest Harbor, Stonington, Swan's Island, Tremont, Isle au Haut, Vinalhaven

Importantly, several other legislators from surrounding areas have also supported the board's
work throughout this time -- a reflection of just how vital this resource was, and still is, to our
broader region. This project is shovel-ready, community-driven, and offers a smart reuse of existing
infrastructure to meet a growing need. The proposed funding will help kick-start renovations, which are expected to cost between $1.2 and $1.5 million. These state dollars will help leverage additional private and federal investments to bring the project to completion.
LD 1106 includes accountability language requiring the Maine State Housing Authority to report
on the use of funds and project progress within six months of receipt. However, based on conversations with the agency, I want to note that this timeline could be adjusted if needed to
better align with departmental operations.
In addition to serving older adults, the creation of 24 new housing units Will help reduce the overall housing burden felt throughout the community. By adding to our limited housing stock,
this project supports both individual stability and regional economic resilience. This bill is about restoring opportunity and dignity for older Mainers in our coastal communities.
I respectfully ask for your support of LD I106, and I would be happy to answer any questions.
District 15: Brooklin, Deer Isle, Eagle Island Township, Frenchboro, Southwest Harbor, Stonington, Swan's Island, Tremont, Isle au Haut, Vinalhaven

Testimony of Senator Nicole Grohoski in support of

Before the Committee on Housing and Economic Development April 1, 2025
Senator Curry, Representative Gere, and members of the Housing and Economic Development Committee. I am Senator Nicole Grohoski, and I represent District 7, the majority of Hancock County - including the towns of Deer Isle and Stonington. Thank you for the opportunity to testify in support of LD 1106, "An Act to Provide Funds for the Redevelopment of the Island Nursing Home in Hancock County into Affordable Senior Housing."
This bill provides a one-time appropriation of $250,000 to support the conversion of the now-closed Island Nursing Home in Deer Isle into 24 affordable apartments for senior citizens. It represents a direct and targeted investment to address a critical shortage of senior housing in a region deeply affected by the loss of long-term care facilities. In addition to this appropriation, the bill ensures transparency and accountability by requiring the Maine State Housing Authority to submit a detailed progress and financial report within six months of receiving the funds.
This is a smart and strategic investment. As you well know, the cost of constructing a single unit of housing can often run well above $250,000 per unit. Yet through this initiative, the state is being asked to contribute just over $11,000 per unit--a fraction of what it would otherwise cost--thanks to the leveraging of additional funds and the commitment of the community. That's a phenomenal deal for Maine taxpayers and an opportunity we should not pass up.
This effort also highlights the strength and resilience of the local community. The board of the Island Nursing Home has stepped up with a compelling vision, and they've brought in outside investment and momentum. While we continue working toward restoring long-term care infrastructure across Maine--and I remain committed to bringing nursing home care back to Hancock County--we must also act now to support intermediate solutions for older residents.
Currently, in my district, there are very few housing options for seniors who wish to downsize and age in place. This creates a bottleneck in our housing system--seniors are remaining in

Senator Curry, Representative Gere, and Members of the Housing and Economic Development Committee. My name is Skip Greenlaw, and I live in Stonington. I am Vice President of the Board of Directors of the island Nursing Home in Deer lsle, now dba as Home Port. l stand before you today in strong support of LD# 1106, An Act To Provide Funds for the Redevelopment of the Island Nursing Home in Hancock County Into Affordable Senior Housing.
I want to thank Rep. Eaton for sponsoring this legislation and to Sen. Grohoski, Rep. Milliken, Rep. Friedmann, and Rep. Ray for co-sponsoring this legislation.
The Island Nursing Home opened in 1983 with 50 skilled and residential care beds with expansion to 70 beds in the
late 19905. We were forced to close in October 2021 due to a lack of adequate staff and the prohibitive cost of contract nursing. We are grateful to the legislature and Governor Mills for making sufficient funds to pay for contract
nursing in hospitals and nursing homes during the Covid pandemic. This shortage of nurses and inadequate
reimbursement has caused the closure of over 40 nursing homes in Maine since 2014. We feel that the State of
Maine has not sufficiently supported the care of the large aging population of Maine.
After closing, the Board tried to reopen as a Residential Care facility, but insufficient funds from donors, endowment
funds, and projected MaineCare reimbursement would leave a yearly financial gap of $500,000.
The decision was made to convert the building to senior housing- converting 2 patient rooms into an apartment with
a bedroom, living room, a kitchenette, and bathroom with a shower. The first apartment is under construction and almost completed at an estimated cost of between
$65,000 to $75,000. We have been told that this is an extremely low price for construction of an apartment in today's economy. We anticipate having 23 units. The building is 42 years old and has been well maintained, but with this
renovation we will make property improvements to insure the comfort and safety for our seniors, including a laundry
room. We will also maintain the common spaces in the building for residents to socialize and have community
functions.
While the senior population is our priority, given the senior housing shortage, we will make some apartments
available to essential workers depending on the senior demand.
While we understand that State resources are very tight, we know that you all consider housing a priority. The investment we are asking you to make for the reconstructed apartments will generate some badly needed housing at
a very reasonable cost per unit. We estimate that we will need to spend close to $2,000,000 to complete the renovation of our patient rooms into 23 apartments. We have $500,000 of our own resources to pay for a portion of the construction. We are currently negotiating a loan with a local bank. We will be conducting a capital campaign as soon as the apartment is completed. We will have a open house shortly to show off the one finished apartment.
